{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01SqTVEJKoS43JmUAAYF3ERu","type":"tool_result","content":"# sco_readout release notes\n\n## 2.3.1 (2026-08-18)\n- `gate` writes `analysis_panel.csv` and `readout.json` in the layout Finance asked for\n  (`docs/outputs/readout_contract.md`).\n\n## 2.3.0 (2026-06-02)\n- Wave-level readout: one treatment indicator per wave in the fixed-effects regression.\n\n## 2.0.0 (2025-11-20)\n- Generalised from the ESL readout: store and week fixed effects, store-clustered standard errors, basket size as the\n  programme KPI.\n# Store KPI handbook (extract)\n\nOwner: Retail Finance. All store KPIs are reported in trading weeks that run **Monday to Sunday**; a week is labelled by\nits Monday (`week_start`).\n\n| KPI | Definition | Source |\n|---|---|---|\n| Net sales | merchandise sales net of returns and promotional markdowns, excluding VAT, lottery and the pharmacy counter | `kpi_store_week.net_sales` |\n| Customer transactions | completed checkout transactions (staffed lanes and self-checkout) | `kpi_store_week.customer_txns` |\n| Basket size | net sales / customer transactions | derived |\n| SCO share | share of customer transactions completed at self-checkout | `kpi_store_week.sco_txn_share` |\n| Pharmacy sales | pharmacy counter sales, reported separately (stores with a pharmacy only) | `kpi_store_week.pharmacy_sales` |\n\n## Comparable trading weeks\n\nA **comparable trading week** is a week in which the store traded its full hours on all seven days. A store-week with\nany record in `store_closures` (install works, weather, refrigeration, power, flooring) is not a comparable trading\nweek. Like-for-like reporting and programme evaluations use comparable trading weeks only; partial weeks are kept in the\nledger for completeness.\n\n## Notes\n\n- Transactions and basket size move in opposite directions when shoppers consolidate trips; net sales is the figure\n  the P&L uses.\n# Finance glossary (Store Investments, extract)\n\n**Uplift.** The change a programme causes in a store's figure: actual, minus what the store would have done over the\nsame weeks without the programme. For sales figures, uplift is expressed in log points (0.025 ≈ 2.5%).\n\n**Run-rate.** Performance once a change has bedded in: weeks 13 to 26 after go-live, counting the go-live week as\nweek 1. Weeks that are not comparable trading weeks (`docs/kpi_handbook.md`) are left out.\n\n**Store-level vs programme-level figures.** A store's run-rate uplift is the average over its run-rate weeks. A\nprogramme-level or wave-level figure is the simple average across the stores concerned (each store counts once,\nwhatever its size), because capital is committed per store.\n\n**Go-live.** The first trading week in which the installed equipment is in customer use.\n\n**Tranche.** A tranche of a staged programme is a set of waves released together.\n# SCO 2.0 business case (approved 2024-11-26, Capital Committee)\n\nSponsor: COO. Finance partner: FP&A (Store Investments).\n\n## 1. What we are buying\n\nSCO 2.0 replaces the self-checkout bank with the new scale-integrated units and, where the building allows it, a\nbig-basket self-checkout lane. Installation is staged in six waves (plan `rollout_plan`, version 2024-11).\n\n| Kit | Capex per store | Maintenance per year |\n|---|---|---|\n| Full (with big-basket lane) | £410k | £22k |\n| Compact | £265k | £15k |\n\n## 2. Why\n\nStore Operations expects faster checkout and larger consolidated shops. The Programme team tracks basket size and SCO\nshare as its programme KPIs.\n\n## 3. Staged capital release and continuation gate\n\nCapital is released in two tranches.\n\n- **Tranche 1 (waves 1–4)** was released at approval.\n- **Tranche 2 (waves 5–6)** is released only if the continuation gate is met: the expected **run-rate uplift in\n  weekly net sales for the stores in waves 5–6, as planned**, is at least **2.5%**. At 2.5% the tranche pays back\n  inside the kit's depreciation life at the planned kit mix; below it, it does not.\n\nThe gate figure is prepared by FP&A from the waves already live and presented to the Capital Committee with its\nuncertainty. Definitions follow the finance glossary (`docs/finance/glossary.md`).\n\n## 4. Out of scope\n\nReverting stores already installed is not considered (the capex is sunk and the kits have no resale value).\n# SCO 2.0 wave sequencing (Store Operations, November 2024)\n\nHow the store list was split into waves for plan version 2024-11.\n\n1. **Readiness first.** Waves 1–2 are weighted towards Supercentres: they have the floor space, the longest staffed\n   queues and dedicated install crews in every region.\n2. **Within a format, stores with a usable rear bagging bay go earlier.** The big-basket lane is the headline feature\n   and those installs are the ones the vendor wanted to prove first; stores without a bay were pushed to later waves.\n3. **Crew geography.** Within those groups, stores were allocated to waves by installer region so that a crew works\n   through neighbouring stores in sequence.\n4. Waves 5–6 hold the remaining stores.\n\nNo store was chosen or deferred because of its sales performance.\n# SCO 2.0 programme brief\n\nOwner: Store Transformation (Programme team). Last updated 2026-09-01.\n\n## The change\n\n- New self-checkout units with integrated scales and faster card readers (all stores).\n- **Big-basket lane**: a self-checkout lane sized for trolley shops, with a bagging area behind the tills. It needs a\n  usable rear bagging bay; the store layout survey (June 2024) recorded which stores have one.\n- Stores with a usable bay get the **full kit** (new units + big-basket lane). Stores without one get the **compact kit**\n  (new units only). The kit is fixed when the store is scheduled and recorded on the work order.\n- The software, screens and staffing model are identical in both kits.\n\n## Installation\n\n1. **Prewire** (overnight, store open) about two to three weeks before go-live.\n2. **Install**: the old bank is removed and the new units and lanes fitted. The store closes for one or two trading\n   days in the week before go-live or the one before that, depending on crew scheduling; larger jobs are split\n   across both weeks.\n3. **Go-live** on a Monday: the new equipment is in customer use from opening. Nothing is visible to customers before\n   go-live.\n\nCrews work to the wave plan, but dates move: supply and crew availability push a share of stores back one to four\nweeks. The install log (`install_log`) records what actually happened; the plan is not updated after release.\n\n## Waves\n\n| Wave | Planned go-live | Status (2026-09) |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | February 2025 | live |\n| 2 | April 2025 | live |\n| 3 | July 2025 | live |\n| 4 | September 2025 | live |\n| 5 | December 2026 | awaiting tranche 2 |\n| 6 | March 2027 | awaiting tranche 2 |\n\n## Assumptions stated at approval\n\n- Stores are at least six miles from their nearest sister store; shoppers lost to a store are assumed to go to\n  competitors or online, not to another Meridian store.\n# Readout output contract (Finance, SCO 2.0 tranche 2)\n\n`python -m sco_readout gate --warehouse <db> --out <dir>` writes two files. Numbers are written unrounded.\n\n## `analysis_panel.csv`\n\nOne row per row of `kpi_store_week` (every store and week in the extract).\n\n| Column | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `store_id`, `week_start` | the store-week |\n| `wave` | the store's wave in the rollout plan |\n| `go_live_week` | `week_start` of the store's go-live week; empty if the store is not live in the extract |\n| `event_week` | weeks from the go-live week to this week (0 in the go-live week, negative before); empty if not live |\n| `comparable` | 1 if the week is a comparable trading week (`docs/kpi_handbook.md`), else 0 |\n| `log_net_sales` | natural log of `net_sales` |\n\n## `readout.json`\n\n```json\n{\n  \"effect_by_wave\": {\"1\": {\"estimate\": 0.0, \"ci_low\": 0.0, \"ci_high\": 0.0}, \"...\": {}},\n  \"gate_effect\": {\"estimate\": 0.0, \"ci_low\": 0.0, \"ci_high\": 0.0},\n  \"decision\": \"continue\"\n}\n```\n\n- `effect_by_wave`: one entry per wave that is live in the extract, keyed by wave number: that wave's stores'\n  run-rate uplift in weekly net sales (`docs/finance/glossary.md`), with a 95% interval.\n- `gate_effect`: the figure the tranche-2 continuation gate is evaluated on (`docs/finance/sco2_business_case.md` §3),\n  with a 95% interval.\n- `decision`: `continue` if `gate_effect.estimate` meets the gate's hurdle, else `stop`.\n\nFigures are in log points.","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1155f59a-e578-4035-9d69-7c3ab6128260","uuid":"1c3b0270-3705-4e01-9e99-0dba315ab5d2","timestamp":"2026-10-01T01:14:38.085Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"# sco_readout release notes\n\n## 2.3.1 (2026-08-18)\n- `gate` writes `analysis_panel.csv` and `readout.json` in the layout Finance asked for\n  (`docs/outputs/readout_contract.md`).\n\n## 2.3.0 (2026-06-02)\n- Wave-level readout: one treatment indicator per wave in the fixed-effects regression.\n\n## 2.0.0 (2025-11-20)\n- Generalised from the ESL readout: store and week fixed effects, store-clustered standard errors, basket size as the\n  programme KPI.\n# Store KPI handbook (extract)\n\nOwner: Retail Finance. Numbers are written unrounded.\n\n## `analysis_panel.csv`\n\nOne row per row of `kpi_store_week` (every store and week in the extract).\n\n| Column | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `store_id`, `week_start` | the store-week |\n| `wave` | the store's wave in the rollout plan |\n| `go_live_week` | `week_start` of the store's go-live week; empty if the store is not live in the extract |\n| `event_week` | weeks from the go-live week to this week (0 in the go-live week, negative before); empty if not live |\n| `comparable` | 1 if the week is a comparable trading week (`docs/kpi_handbook.md`), else 0 |\n| `log_net_sales` | natural log of `net_sales` |\n\n## `readout.json`\n\n```json\n{\n  \"effect_by_wave\": {\"1\": {\"estimate\": 0.0, \"ci_low\": 0.0, \"ci_high\": 0.0}, \"...\": {}},\n  \"gate_effect\": {\"estimate\": 0.0, \"ci_low\": 0.0, \"ci_high\": 0.0},\n  \"decision\": \"continue\"\n}\n```\n\n- `effect_by_wave`: one entry per wave that is live in the extract, keyed by wave number: that wave's stores'\n  run-rate uplift in weekly net sales (`docs/finance/glossary.md`), with a 95% interval.\n- `gate_effect`: the figure the tranche-2 continuation gate is evaluated on (`docs/finance/sco2_business_case.md` §3),\n  with a 95% interval.\n- `decision`: `continue` if `gate_effect.estimate` meets the gate's hurdle, else `stop`.\n\nFigures are in log points.","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01EieTgmfNrtRMgjcezseabT","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Store-programme readouts (Store Analytics). Release 2.3.1.\"\"\"\n__version__ = \"2.3.1\"\nfrom sco_readout.cli import main\n\nmain()\n\"\"\"`python -m sco_readout gate --warehouse data/warehouse.sqlite --out out/`\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom sco_readout import estimate, panel, report\n\n\ndef gate(warehouse: Path, out: Path) -> None:\n    p = panel.build(warehouse)\n    by_wave = estimate.twfe_by_wave(p, outcome=\"log_basket\")\n    overall = estimate.twfe(p, outcome=\"log_basket\")\n    report.write_all(out, p, by_wave, overall)\n\n\ndef main(argv=None) -> None:\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"sco_readout\")\n    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    g = sub.add_parser(\"gate\", help=\"programme readout and continuation-gate figure\")\n    g.add_argument(\"--warehouse\", default=\"data/warehouse.sqlite\")\n    g.add_argument(\"--out\", default=\"out\")\n    args = ap.parse_args(argv)\n    gate(Path(args.warehouse), Path(args.out))\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n\"\"\"Panel regression with store and week fixed effects (house method since the ESL readout).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\n\n\ndef _demean(df: pd.DataFrame, cols, iters: int = 50) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    out = df[cols].astype(float).copy()\n    for _ in range(iters):\n        out -= out.groupby(df[\"store_id\"]).transform(\"mean\")\n        out -= out.groupby(df[\"week_start\"]).transform(\"mean\")\n    return out\n\n\ndef _fit(df: pd.DataFrame, y: str, xs) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:\n    d = df[df[\"comparable\"] == 1]\n    dm = _demean(d, [y] + list(xs))\n    X, Y = dm[list(xs)].to_numpy(), dm[y].to_numpy()\n    beta = np.linalg.lstsq(X, Y, rcond=None)[0]\n    resid = Y - X @ beta\n    bread = np.linalg.inv(X.T @ X)\n    meat = np.zeros((len(xs), len(xs)))\n    for _, idx in d.groupby(\"store_id\").indices.items():\n        g = X[idx].T @ resid[idx]\n        meat += np.outer(g, g)\n    vcov = bread @ meat @ bread\n    return beta, np.sqrt(np.diag(vcov))\n\n\ndef twfe(panel: pd.DataFrame, outcome: str) -> dict:\n    beta, se = _fit(panel, outcome, [\"treated\"])\n    return {\"estimate\": float(beta[0]), \"se\": float(se[0])}\n\n\ndef twfe_by_wave(panel: pd.DataFrame, outcome: str) -> dict:\n    p = panel.copy()\n    waves = sorted(p.loc[p[\"go_live_week\"].notna(), \"wave\"].unique())\n    xs = []\n    for w in waves:\n        col = f\"treated_w{w}\"\n        p[col] = ((p[\"wave\"] == w) & (p[\"treated\"] == 1)).astype(int)\n        xs.append(col)\n    beta, se = _fit(p, outcome, xs)\n    return {str(int(w)): {\"estimate\": float(b), \"se\": float(s)} for w, b, s in zip(waves, beta, se)}\n\"\"\"Store x week analysis panel from the warehouse.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\n\n\ndef connect(db: Path) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n    return sqlite3.connect(f\"file:{Path(db).resolve()}?mode=ro\", uri=True)\n\n\ndef build(db: Path) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    con = connect(db)\n    try:\n        kpi = pd.read_sql_query(\"SELECT store_id, week_start, net_sales, customer_txns FROM kpi_store_week\", con)\n        plan = pd.read_sql_query(\"SELECT store_id, wave, planned_go_live FROM rollout_plan\", con)\n    finally:\n        con.close()\n    p = kpi.merge(plan, on=\"store_id\", how=\"left\")\n    last_week = p[\"week_start\"].max()\n    live = p[\"planned_go_live\"] <= last_week\n    p[\"go_live_week\"] = p[\"planned_go_live\"].where(live)\n    weeks = (pd.to_datetime(p[\"week_start\"]) - pd.to_datetime(p[\"go_live_week\"])).dt.days // 7\n    p[\"event_week\"] = weeks.astype(\"Int64\")\n    p[\"comparable\"] = (p[\"customer_txns\"] > 0).astype(int)\n    p[\"log_net_sales\"] = np.log(p[\"net_sales\"])\n    p[\"log_basket\"] = np.log(p[\"net_sales\"] / p[\"customer_txns\"])\n    p[\"treated\"] = (p[\"event_week\"].fillna(-1) >= 0).astype(int)\n    return p.sort_values([\"store_id\", \"week_start\"]).reset_index(drop=True)\n\"\"\"Readout files (docs/outputs/readout_contract.md).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pandas as pd\n\nHURDLE = 0.025          # continuation hurdle, business case section 3\nPANEL_COLS = [\"store_id\", \"week_start\", \"wave\", \"go_live_week\", \"event_week\", \"comparable\", \"log_net_sales\"]\n\n\ndef _ci(e: dict) -> dict:\n    return {\"estimate\": e[\"estimate\"], \"ci_low\": e[\"estimate\"] - 1.96 * e[\"se\"],\n            \"ci_high\": e[\"estimate\"] + 1.96 * e[\"se\"]}\n\n\ndef write_all(out: Path, panel: pd.DataFrame, by_wave: dict, overall: dict) -> None:\n    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    panel[PANEL_COLS].to_csv(out / \"analysis_panel.csv\", index=False)\n    gate = _ci(overall)\n    readout = {\n        \"effect_by_wave\": {w: _ci(e) for w, e in by_wave.items()},\n        \"gate_effect\": gate,\n        \"decision\": \"continue\" if gate[\"estimate\"] >= HURDLE else \"stop\",\n    }\n    (out / \"readout.json\").write_text(json.dumps(readout, indent=2) + \"\\n\")\n{\n  \"effect_by_wave\": {\n    \"1\": {\n      \"estimate\": 0.08035592227081077,\n      \"ci_low\": 0.07487559591320463,\n      \"ci_high\": 0.08583624862841692\n    },\n    \"2\": {\n      \"estimate\": 0.06019394101288629,\n      \"ci_low\": 0.05399611064340431,\n      \"ci_high\": 0.06639177138236828\n    },\n    \"3\": {\n      \"estimate\": 0.04752895485760626,\n      \"ci_low\": 0.04126023029063773,\n      \"ci_high\": 0.05379767942457479\n    },\n    \"4\": {\n      \"estimate\": 0.025764921302665587,\n      \"ci_low\": 0.019446068562135176,\n      \"ci_high\": 0.032083774043196\n    }\n  },\n  \"gate_effect\": {\n    \"estimate\": 0.05523797433269851,\n    \"ci_low\": 0.0519597027100275,\n    \"ci_high\": 0.05851624595536952\n  },\n  \"decision\": \"continue\"\n}\nstore_id,week_start,wave,go_live_week,event_week,comparable,log_net_sales\nS0001,2023-09-04,2,2025-04-28,-86,1,12.411277455433193\nS0001,2023-09-11,2,2025-04-28,-85,1,12.404158990797894\nS0001,2023-09-18,2,2025-04-28,-84,1,12.405007066357701\nS0001,2023-09-25,2,2025-04-28,-83,1,12.395077651570697","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1155f59a-e578-4035-9d69-7c3ab6128260","uuid":"ffe42eb5-469d-445f-84ba-7d8f2fca3b29","timestamp":"2026-10-01T01:14:39.586Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"\"\"\"Store-programme readouts (Store Analytics). 1.96 * e[\"se\"],\n            \"ci_high\": e[\"estimate\"] + 1.96 * e[\"se\"]}\n\n\ndef write_all(out: Path, panel: pd.DataFrame, by_wave: dict, overall: dict) -> None:\n    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    panel[PANEL_COLS].to_csv(out / \"analysis_panel.csv\", index=False)\n    gate = _ci(overall)\n    readout = {\n        \"effect_by_wave\": {w: _ci(e) for w, e in by_wave.items()},\n        \"gate_effect\": gate,\n        \"decision\": \"continue\" if gate[\"estimate\"] >= HURDLE else \"stop\",\n    }\n    (out / \"readout.json\").write_text(json.dumps(readout, indent=2) + \"\\n\")\n{\n  \"effect_by_wave\": {\n    \"1\": {\n      \"estimate\": 0.08035592227081077,\n      \"ci_low\": 0.07487559591320463,\n      \"ci_high\": 0.08583624862841692\n    },\n    \"2\": {\n      \"estimate\": 0.06019394101288629,\n      \"ci_low\": 0.05399611064340431,\n      \"ci_high\": 0.06639177138236828\n    },\n    \"3\": {\n      \"estimate\": 0.04752895485760626,\n      \"ci_low\": 0.04126023029063773,\n      \"ci_high\": 0.05379767942457479\n    },\n    \"4\": {\n      \"estimate\": 0.025764921302665587,\n      \"ci_low\": 0.019446068562135176,\n      \"ci_high\": 0.032083774043196\n    }\n  },\n  \"gate_effect\": {\n    \"estimate\": 0.05523797433269851,\n    \"ci_low\": 0.0519597027100275,\n    \"ci_high\": 0.05851624595536952\n  },\n  \"decision\": \"continue\"\n}\nstore_id,week_start,wave,go_live_week,event_week,comparable,log_net_sales\nS0001,2023-09-04,2,2025-04-28,-86,1,12.411277455433193\nS0001,2023-09-11,2,2025-04-28,-85,1,12.404158990797894\nS0001,2023-09-18,2,2025-04-28,-84,1,12.405007066357701\nS0001,2023-09-25,2,2025-04-28,-83,1,12.395077651570697","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false}}

pd.to_timedelta(d.dt.dayofweek, unit=\"D\")\n\n\ndef build(db: Path) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    con = connect(db)\n    try:\n        kpi = pd.read_sql_query(\"SELECT store_id, week_start, net_sales, customer_txns FROM kpi_store_week\", con)\n        stores = pd.read_sql_query(\"SELECT store_id, format FROM stores\", con)\n        plan = pd.read_sql_query(\"SELECT store_id, wave, planned_go_live, planned_kit FROM rollout_plan\", con)\n        log = pd.read_sql_query(\"SELECT store_id, event, event_date, kit FROM install_log\", con)\n        closures = pd.read_sql_query(\"SELECT store_id, closure_date FROM store_closures\", con)\n    finally:\n        con.close()\n\n    kpi[\"week\"] = pd.to_datetime(kpi[\"week_start\"])\n    last_week = kpi[\"week\"].max()\n\n    # Go-live as it actually happened (install log), not as planned; first go-live if a store has several.\n    gl = log[log[\"event\"] == \"go_live\"].copy()\n    gl[\"go_live\"] = _week_of(gl[\"event_date\"])\n    gl = gl.sort_values([\"store_id\", \"go_live\", \"kit\"]).drop_duplicates(\"store_id\")\n    gl = gl[gl[\"go_live\"] <= last_week]\n    # First pre-go-live works (prewire / install) for each live store: from then on a week is not a clean baseline.\n    works = log[log[\"event\"].isin([\"prewire\", \"install\"])].copy()\n    works[\"works\"] = _week_of(works[\"event_date\"])\n    first_works = works.groupby(\"store_id\")[\"works\"].min()\n\n    p = kpi.merge(stores, on=\"store_id\", how=\"left\").merge(plan, on=\"store_id\", how=\"left\")\n    p = p.merge(gl[[\"store_id\", \"go_live\", \"kit\"]], on=\"store_id\", how=\"left\")\n    p[\"works_start\"] = p[\"store_id\"].map(first_works)\n    p[\"works_start\"] = p[[\"works_start\", \"go_live\"]].min(axis=1).where(p[\"go_live\"].notna())\n    p[\"go_live_week\"] = p[\"go_live\"].dt.strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d\")\n    p[\"event_week\"] = ((p[\"week\"] - p[\"go_live\"]).dt.days // 7).astype(\"Int64\")\n    p[\"kit\"] = p[\"kit\"].fillna(p[\"planned_kit\"])\n\n    # Comparable trading week: no closure record of any kind in the store-week (KPI handbook).\n    cw = pd.DataFrame({\"store_id\": closures[\"store_id\"], \"week\": _week_of(closures[\"closure_date\"])}).drop_duplicates()\n    cw[\"closed\"] = 1\n    p = p.merge(cw, on=[\"store_id\", \"week\"], how=\"left\")\n    p[\"comparable\"] = p[\"closed\"].isna().astype(int)\n\n    p[\"log_net_sales\"] = np.log(p[\"net_sales\"])\n    p[\"log_basket\"] = np.log(p[\"net_sales\"] / p[\"customer_txns\"])\n    p[\"treated\"] = (p[\"event_week\"].fillna(-1) >= 0).astype(int)\n    # Baseline weeks: before any install works at a store that goes live, or any week at a store not live.\n    p[\"baseline\"] = (p[\"go_live\"].isna() | (p[\"week\"] < p[\"works_start\"])).astype(int)\n    p = p.drop(columns=[\"week\", \"go_live\", \"works_start\", \"closed\"])\n    return p.sort_values([\"store_id\", \"week_start\"]).reset_index(drop=True)\nEOF"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":870,"cache_read_input_tokens":44747,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":870,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1155f59a-e578-4035-9d69-7c3ab6128260","uuid":"724c30c6-bd43-4222-b6a8-8e396020f537","timestamp":"2026-10-01T01:17:47.034Z","request_id":"req_011CfadmC1hF6KFBDNfJCxfo"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfadpBazFfYrEvcv5tCa5","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01FCAWHQr8DpL7dUqTp9Hc4y","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat > sco_readout/estimate.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"Run-rate uplift by imputation (store and format-by-week effects fitted on baseline weeks).\n\nFor each live store, the counterfactual for a post-go-live week is the store's own level plus the week's level for\nstores of the same format, both estimated only on baseline weeks (stores not yet live, before any install works, and\nstores not live in the extract). Only comparable trading weeks are used. A store's run-rate uplift is its mean\nactual-minus-counterfactual over comparable run-rate weeks; wave and programme figures are simple averages over stores\n(docs/finance/glossary.md). Intervals come from a store-clustered bootstrap of the whole procedure.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\n\nRUN_RATE_WEEKS = (13, 26)   # weeks after go-live, go-live week = week 1 (glossary: run-rate)\nGATE_WAVES = (5, 6)         # tranche 2 (business case section 3)\nN_BOOT = 999\nSEED = 20261001\n\n\ndef _fe_fit(y, s, c, w, ns, nc, a0=None, l0=None, iters=2000, tol=1e-11):\n    \"\"\"Weighted least squares of y on store and cell-week effects by alternating projections.\"\"\"\n    ws = np.bincount(s, w, ns)\n    wc = np.bincount(c, w, nc)\n    a = np.zeros(ns) if a0 is None else a0.copy()\n    l = np.zeros(nc) if l0 is None else l0.copy()\n    for _ in range(iters):\n        a_new = np.bincount(s, w * (y - l[c]), ns) / np.where(ws > 0, ws, 1)\n        l_new = np.bincount(c, w * (y - a_new[s]), nc) / np.where(wc > 0, wc, 1)\n        step = max(np.abs(a_new - a).max(), np.abs(l_new - l).max())\n        a, l = a_new, l_new\n        if step < tol:\n            break\n    a[ws == 0] = np.nan\n    l[wc == 0] = np.nan\n    return a, l\n\n\nclass Design:\n    \"\"\"Arrays for the imputation, built once and reused across bootstrap draws.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, panel: pd.DataFrame, outcome: str = \"log_net_sales\"):\n        p = panel[panel[\"comparable\"] == 1]\n        p = p[np.isfinite(p[outcome])]\n        self.stores, s = np.unique(p[\"store_id\"].to_numpy(), return_inverse=True)\n        cells = p[\"format\"].fillna(\"\").astype(str) + \"|\" + p[\"week_start\"].astype(str)\n        _, c = np.unique(cells.to_numpy(), return_inverse=True)\n        self.ns, self.nc = len(self.stores), int(c.max()) + 1\n        y = p[outcome].to_numpy(float)\n        base = p[\"baseline\"].to_numpy() == 1\n        ev = p[\"event_week\"].to_numpy(dtype=float, na_value=np.nan)\n        lo, hi = RUN_RATE_WEEKS\n        rr = (ev >= lo - 1) & (ev <= hi - 1)\n        self.y_b, self.s_b, self.c_b = y[base], s[base], c[base]\n        self.y_r, self.s_r, self.c_r = y[rr], s[rr], c[rr]\n        self.a0 = self.l0 = None\n\n    def store_uplift(self, sw: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"Run-rate uplift per store (NaN where not estimable) for store weights `sw`.\"\"\"\n        a, l = _fe_fit(self.y_b, self.s_b, self.c_b, sw[self.s_b], self.ns, self.nc, self.a0, self.l0)\n        if self.a0 is None:\n            self.a0, self.l0 = np.nan_to_num(a), np.nan_to_num(l)\n        tau = self.y_r - a[self.s_r] - l[self.c_r]\n        ok = np.isfinite(tau)\n        tot = np.bincount(self.s_r[ok], tau[ok], self.ns)\n        n = np.bincount(self.s_r[ok], minlength=self.ns)\n        return np.where(n > 0, tot / np.where(n > 0, n, 1), np.nan)\n\n\ndef _stores(panel: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    return panel.groupby(\"store_id\")[[\"wave\", \"format\", \"kit\", \"planned_kit\", \"go_live_week\"]].first()\n\n\ndef _figures(tau: pd.Series, sw: pd.Series, info: pd.DataFrame, waves, targets: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:\n    d = info.loc[tau.index].assign(tau=tau, w=sw.loc[tau.index])\n    d = d[np.isfinite(d[\"tau\"]) & (d[\"w\"] > 0)]\n\n    def wmean(x):\n        return float(np.average(x[\"tau\"], weights=x[\"w\"])) if len(x) else np.nan\n\n    out = {f\"w{w}\": wmean(d[d[\"wave\"] == w]) for w in waves}\n    # Gate: each planned tranche-2 store gets the mean uplift of live stores with the same kit and format\n    # (falling back to same kit, then all live stores), and the gate figure is the simple average over them.\n    by_cell = {key: wmean(g) for key, g in d.groupby([\"kit\", \"format\"])}\n    by_kit = {key: wmean(g) for key, g in d.groupby(\"kit\")}\n    overall = wmean(d)\n    pred = [\n        by_cell.get((kit, fmt), np.nan) if np.isfinite(by_cell.get((kit, fmt), np.nan))\n        else by_kit.get(kit, overall) if np.isfinite(by_kit.get(kit, np.nan)) else overall\n        for kit, fmt in zip(targets[\"planned_kit\"], targets[\"format\"])\n    ]\n    out[\"gate\"] = float(np.mean(pred)) if len(pred) else np.nan\n    return out\n\n\ndef readout(panel: pd.DataFrame, outcome: str = \"log_net_sales\", n_boot: int = N_BOOT, seed: int = SEED) -> dict:\n    des = Design(panel, outcome)\n    info = _stores(panel).loc[des.stores]\n    live = info[\"go_live_week\"].notna()\n    waves = sorted(int(w) for w in info.loc[live, \"wave\"].dropna().unique())\n    plan = _stores(panel)\n    targets = plan[plan[\"wave\"].isin(GATE_WAVES)]\n\n    def run(sw):\n        tau = pd.Series(des.store_uplift(sw), index=des.stores)[live.to_numpy()]\n        return _figures(tau, pd.Series(sw, index=des.stores), info, waves, targets)\n\n    point = run(np.ones(des.ns))\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n    draws = [run(rng.multinomial(des.ns, np.full(des.ns, 1.0 / des.ns)).astype(float)) for _ in range(n_boot)]\n    draws = pd.DataFrame(draws)\n\n    def ci(key):\n        b = draws[key].dropna()\n        lo, hi = (np.quantile(b, [0.025, 0.975]) if len(b) else (np.nan, np.nan))\n        return {\"estimate\": point[key], \"ci_low\": float(lo), \"ci_high\": float(hi)}\n\n    return {\"by_wave\": {str(w): ci(f\"w{w}\") for w in waves}, \"gate\": ci(\"gate\")}\nEOF\ncat > sco_readout/report.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"Readout files (docs/outputs/readout_contract.md).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport math\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pandas as pd\n\nHURDLE = 0.025          # continuation hurdle, business case section 3\nPANEL_COLS = [\"store_id\", \"week_start\", \"wave\", \"go_live_week\", \"event_week\", \"comparable\", \"log_net_sales\"]\n\n\ndef _num(x):\n    return None if x is None or (isinstance(x, float) and not math.isfinite(x)) else x\n\n\ndef write_all(out: Path, panel: pd.DataFrame, result: dict) -> None:\n    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    panel[PANEL_COLS].to_csv(out / \"analysis_panel.csv\", index=False)\n    clean = lambda e: {k: _num(v) for k, v in e.items()}\n    gate = clean(result[\"gate\"])\n    readout = {\n        \"effect_by_wave\": {w: clean(e) for w, e in result[\"by_wave\"].items()},\n        \"gate_effect\": gate,\n        \"decision\": \"continue\" if gate[\"estimate\"] is not None and gate[\"estimate\"] >= HURDLE else \"stop\",\n    }\n    (out / \"readout.json\").write_text(json.dumps(readout, indent=2) + \"\\n\")\nEOF\npython - <<'EOF'\nimport re\nf='sco_readout/cli.py'; s=open(f).read()\ns=s.replace('''    by_wave = estimate.twfe_by_wave(p, outcome=\"log_basket\")\n    overall = estimate.twfe(p, outcome=\"log_basket\")\n    report.write_all(out, p, by_wave, overall)''','''    result = estimate.readout(p, outcome=\"log_net_sales\")\n    report.write_all(out, p, result)''')\nopen(f,'w').write(s)\nEOF\ncd /workspace && time python -m sco_readout gate --warehouse data/warehouse.sqlite --out out && cat out/readout.json && md5sum out/*"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3906,"cache_read_input_tokens":45617,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":3906,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1155f59a-e578-4035-9d69-7c3ab6128260","uuid":"6f048eff-aad4-4fa4-ba99-91765a6dd535","timestamp":"2026-10-01T01:18:21.051Z","request_id":"req_011CfadpB1W9fvPGKK3KQtD7"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfadyk85K8jJpoWjv6kaD","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've rebuilt the gate figure. The readout now puts it at **+1.0% (95% CI +0.9% to +1.2%)**, against a 2.5% hurdle, so the recommendation is **not to release tranche 2 on the current plan**.\n\nThe required command now writes `out/analysis_panel.csv` and `out/readout.json` to the contract. Two runs on this extract gave byte-identical outputs, and a run takes about 40 seconds.\n\n| Wave | Run-rate net sales uplift | 95% CI |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | +4.1% | +3.7% to +4.4% |\n| 2 | +3.5% | +3.1% to +3.9% |\n| 3 | +3.1% | +2.7% to +3.6% |\n| 4 | +1.9% | +1.5% to +2.3% |\n| **Gate (waves 5–6 as planned)** | **+1.0%** | **+0.9% to +1.2%** |\n\n**What drives it:** the kit, not the wave. At run-rate, full-kit stores (with the big-basket lane) are up about 4.2–4.4% in every format and every wave. Compact-kit stores are flat to slightly down (−0.3%). The waves don't differ because shoppers are \"learning the lane\"; the later waves just have more compact kits. Waves 5–6 as planned are 71% compact kit, mostly Neighbourhood stores, so their expected uplift is about 1%. This matches what Store Operations is hearing: customer transactions fall 1–1.5% under both kits, so basket size rises everywhere while net sales only rise where the big-basket lane is fitted.\n\n**How it's estimated (for the Committee):**\n- Each live store is compared with what it would have done without SCO 2.0. That baseline is its own pre-install level plus the week-by-week movement of same-format stores that aren't live yet.\n- Pre-go-live trends are flat, and there's no sign that installs took sales from stores not yet installed.\n- Only comparable trading weeks are used, and the uplift is measured over weeks 13–26 after the actual go-live.\n- Each store counts once.\n- The gate gives each planned waves 5–6 store the average uplift of live stores with the same kit and format.\n- Intervals come from resampling whole stores.\n- The result is unchanged when the comparison is made within region as well as format.\n- The interval reflects estimation uncertainty only. It assumes future compact-kit stores will behave like the 135 already live.\n\n**Why the earlier figures shouldn't go to the Committee:**\n1. **Programme readout (basket +5.5%):** basket size isn't the gate measure. It rises partly because transactions fall.\n2. **FP&A notebook (net sales +6.7%):** it reused the same flawed method. It:\n   - took go-live dates from the plan rather than the install log (a quarter of stores were up to four weeks late);\n   - counted closure weeks, including install-works weeks, as normal trading;\n   - averaged over every week from go-live instead of the run-rate window;\n   - weighted stores by how many weeks they contributed rather than counting each once.\n   \n   Above all, its single regression compared stores across formats. Over this period Supercentres grew about 10% a year on their own and Neighbourhood stores shrank about 4% a year, and early waves were heavy in Supercentres, so format growth was counted as programme effect.\n3. **Both** quoted the average for waves 1–4, but the gate is defined on the waves 5–6 stores, which are mostly compact kit.\n\nThe changes are in `sco_readout/panel.py`, `sco_readout/estimate.py`, `sco_readout/report.py` and `sco_readout/cli.py`. The method contains nothing tied to particular stores, waves or dates in this extract. The only fixed inputs are business-case definitions: the 2.5% hurdle, weeks 13–26, and waves 5–6 as tranche 2. The warehouse and reports are untouched. The FP&A notebook no longer runs, because it called the old regression functions, which I removed.\n\nA full-kit-only tranche (stores with a usable bagging bay) would clear 2.5% on these numbers. That would be a new proposal for the Committee, not the gate as approved."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1196,"cache_read_input_tokens":54260,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":1196,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1155f59a-e578-4035-9d69-7c3ab6128260","uuid":"664e2b96-8f4e-4d3b-9a2e-63a1d6a7d088","timestamp":"2026-10-01T01:20:13.940Z","request_id":"req_011CfadyjZ6vUngo3jKDPoRx"}
